cards.explanation: The answer is an expert in the law. The text says one of the Pharisees, "…an expert in the law…" tested Jesus with a question (Matthew 22:35). I bet a man like that walked up feeling ready. He brought a test to the Teacher, and friends, that is a BOLD move.

The answer is love the Lord your God. Jesus says, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." Then He adds, "This is the first and greatest commandment." The man asked which one is greatest, and Jesus names it plainly. I love a clear answer.

The answer is all. Jesus says to love the Lord your God "…with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." Notice He says "all" three times. That's no leftovers and no halfway, and I'm still working on my own batch of that.

The second commandment is to love your neighbor as yourself. Jesus says, "And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’" He says it's like the first, so these two belong together. The man asked for one commandment and got a pair. Not bad for one question!

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't call these two small at all. He calls the first "…the first and greatest commandment." and says the second "…is like it…" Then He says, "All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments." So these two hold up everything else.

The answer is David. Jesus asks whose son the Christ is, and the Pharisees answer, "David's." David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and in a moment Jesus brings up what David said in the Spirit. Keep that answer in your pocket, friends, because Jesus is about to use it.

The answer is the Christ. Jesus asks, "How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’?" The "Him" is the Christ, the one the Pharisees just said is David's son. David says, "The Lord said to my Lord…" so he's calling that person his Lord. That's why the question lands so hard.

The puzzle is that David would be calling his own son Lord. The Pharisees say the Christ is David's son, and then David calls Him "Lord." Jesus asks, "So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?" Then the text says, "No one was able to answer a word…" (Matthew 22:46).
The answer is True. The text says, "No one was able to answer a word…" These were the same Pharisees who gathered together to question Jesus. Now they've got nothing to say.

The answer is that no one dares to question Jesus any further. The text says, "…from that day on no one dared to question Him any further." The Pharisees had gathered to test Jesus, and now no one dares. Right before that, "No one was able to answer a word…" (Matthew 22:46).
